name: CoRL — Conference on Robot Learning
notes: The top venue for robot learning. Single-track, very strong networking. Sellouts are common.

name: IROS — IEEE/RSJ Intelligent Robots & Systems
ticketNote: IEEE student early $460, student non-member $520, member $920
notes: 'Roboburgh' — biggest general robotics conference (7k+ attendees). Book early for hotels.

name: ICRA — IEEE Robotics & Automation
notes: Flagship IEEE robotics conference. 2027 edition in Tokyo.

name: RSS — Robotics: Science & Systems
notes: Single-track, highly selective — the premier place to see frontier robotics & ML work.

name: ROSCon Global
ticketNote: Early student $250 / general $575; late student $500 / general $1025; workshops +$50–150
notes: The ROS/ROS2 community event — best place for robotics software engineers & interns. Often sells out.

name: ROSCon UK
notes: Compact, cheap, genuinely friendly UK ROS gathering with workshops and tours.

name: IEEE-RAS Humanoids
notes: All humanoid robotics — worth it if you build legged or bipedal systems.

name: European Robotics Forum (ERF)
notes: European robotics ecosystem meet — heavy industry presence, lots of internship recruiting.

name: RoboBusiness
ticketNote: Commercial robotics expo — free exhibit floor usually
notes: Robotics industry, investors, and startups — great for startup internship hunting.

name: Automate
ticketNote: Exhibit-only entry often free; conference paid
notes: North America's largest industrial automation show — logistics, AMRs, cobots, factory AI.

name: Robotics Summit & Expo
notes: Deep-dive robotics engineering talks across hardware, safety, and autonomy.

name: Hannover Messe
notes: World's biggest industrial trade fair — every industrial robot OEM exhibits.

name: NVIDIA GTC
ticketNote: Digital pass free; in-person often $100–500 with early-bird
notes: GPU + accelerated computing + robotics (Isaac/Omniverse). Student pass is very cheap.

name: AUVSI XPONENTIAL
notes: Drones, UAS, autonomy expo — massive vendor floor for autonomy jobs.

name: CPS-IoT Week
notes: The 'physics-meets-systems' crowd — IoT, real-time, robotics control.

name: RoboCup World Championship
notes: Robot soccer World Cup — teams of undergrads from 45+ countries. Great for joining a team.

name: RoboGames
notes: 40+ robot contest categories under one roof — combat bots, sumo, maze, LEGO. Hidden gem.

name: FIRST Championship
notes: 80k-person robotics festival (FRC finale). Alumni network is unmatched.

name: VEX Robotics World Championship
notes: World's largest robotics competition by team count.

name: NHRL — National Havoc Robot League
notes: Welterweight combat bot league — the hidden gem of fight robotics. Very DIY-friendly.

name: BattleBots (spectator)
notes: Heavyweight combat robots. Team spots for students are scarce — spectating is easy.

name: RoboSub
notes: Autonomous underwater robotics — college teams, funded by sponsors.

name: Eurobot
notes: Amateur/student robot builders across Europe — very approachable teams.

name: Robofest
notes: RIT-run autonomous robotics competition with an easy regional on-ramp.

name: NeurIPS
notes: The AI conference. 2026 is multi-site (Sydney + Atlanta + Paris). Career fair is enormous.

name: ICML
notes: Core ML conference — papers, career fair, and industry recruiting all week.

name: ICLR
notes: Open-review ML conference, heavy on deep learning & LLM research.

name: AAAI
notes: Premier general AI conference with strong student outreach programs.

name: CVPR
ticketNote: Student non-member early $625, IEEE student $525, general $900–1200
notes: Computer vision flagship. Huge expo + demo hall for startups.

name: ICCV
notes: Vision conference on even years (next: 2028). Big industry presence.

name: ECCV
notes: European vision conference on odd years (next: 2027).

name: ACL
notes: Core NLP/LLM research venue.

name: EMNLP
notes: LLMs, NLP systems, and heavy industry recruiting for applied ML roles.

name: KDD
notes: Applied ML + data science venue. Strong at catching start-up MLEs.

name: SIGGRAPH
notes: Graphics, simulation, render, and embodied AI. The expo is spectacular.

name: MLOps World
notes: Practical ML infra. Great for spotting free-agent startups hiring interns.

name: TinyML Summit
notes: Microcontrollers + ML — where robotics sensors and model quantization collide.

name: CppCon
ticketNote: Student $399 only; regular $2299–3099; Friday sessions free without registration
notes: The C++ conference. Student ticket is a steal. Run by CppCon volunteers.

name: C++Now
notes: C++ template/metaprogramming mecca at Aspen — small, intense, unforgettable.

name: KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA
notes: Cloud-native infrastructure. Free co-located events + huge expo.

name: KubeCon EU
notes: European cloud-native counterpart to KubeCon NA.

name: PyCon US
notes: The friendly giant. Massive tutorials + expo. Student sprints ideal for open-source.

name: EuroPython
notes: Community-run Python conference, budget-friendly.

name: FOSDEM
notes: Story of free-software devrooms, 800+ talks, zero cost. Bring a USB-C charger and water.

name: Linux Plumbers Conference
notes: Kernel & systems devroom-style micro-confs. Watch for GSoC students.

name: USENIX ATC / OSDI
notes: Systems research — OS, storage, networking. Academia-heavy.

name: SPLASH / OOPSLA
notes: Where programming-language and software-design research meets industry.

name: CAV / PLDI (formal methods)
notes: Program verification + safety-critical robotics; small community, big hiring.

name: LLVM Developers' Meeting
notes: Compiler engineering — chip and ML teams recruit tooling folks here.

name: EuroSys / SOSP
notes: Systems research superconference. Golden networking for distributed systems.

name: Supercomputing (SC)
ticketNote: HPC/supercomputing conf; student day + travel grants
notes: Compute + data-center infrastructure. Buckets of accelerator startups.

name: CIDR (databases)
notes: The 'cool kids' database systems conference — signaling to DB/vector startups.

name: SIGMOD / VLDB
notes: Database research + industry — good for vector DB and data-infra folks.

name: Google I/O
notes: Google's dev conference — free livestreams, in-person ticket lottery.

name: Microsoft Build
notes: Azure/.NET/AI dev conference.

name: WWDC (Apple)
notes: Apple's developer conference (invite/lottery). The student scholarship program covers travel.

name: AWS re:Invent
notes: AWS's 60k-attendee conference. Insane scale; expo worth it alone.

name: Embedded World
notes: Embedded/microcontrollers/RTOS — combine with a German tech visit.

name: RISC-V Summit
notes: RISC-V cores, AI accelerators, and the hottest chip startup scene.

name: Hot Chips
notes: Where chip architects present new silicon — AMD/Intel/Nvidia folks recruit here.

name: Go / Rust / Zig community confs
notes: RustConf, GopherCon, Zig, OCaml — cheap and full of OSS builders.

name: Black Hat USA
notes: Corporate security conference. Expensive but the expo + hiring fair is deep.

name: DEF CON
ticketNote: Cash at door $520 (LineCon); online $560–600 + CC fee
notes: The hacker pilgrimage after Black Hat. Bring cash, a burner laptop, and a great story.

name: BSides (major cities)
notes: Community-run security confs the week before DEF CON. Hidden-network goldmines.

name: RSA Conference
notes: Giant of infosec. The exhibit hall is huge for networking.

name: GDC — Game Developers Conference
notes: Game dev show — useful if you build graphics/real-time simulators.

name: SmallSat Conference
notes: CubeSats, lunar landers, on-orbit computing. Space robotics recruit here.

name: Space Symposium
ticketNote: Expensive corporate show; student passes exist
notes: Defense/space establishment — Lockheed, Raytheon, SpaceX presence.

name: NASA Human Exploration Rover Challenge
notes: Design a human-powered rover. Mechanical + controls + software teams.

name: DAC — Design Automation Conference
notes: EDA, RTL, FPGA, ML-at-the-edge designers and chip startups.

name: QuantCon
notes: NYC quant scene — networking with funds is very direct.

name: NYC quant meetups
notes: Check NYC/London quant meetups — cheaper access to the trading world than conferences.

name: HackMIT
ticketNote: Free for accepted students; travel reimbursements available
notes: MIT's flagship 1000+ student hackathon. Apply by early July.

name: PennApps
ticketNote: Free for accepted; travel reimbursement up to a cap
notes: 48-hour college hackathon, 1000+ students.

name: TreeHacks (Stanford)
ticketNote: Free for accepted; travel support limited
notes: Stanford's elite 36-hour hardware + AI hackathon.

name: Cal Hacks
notes: Berkeley's fall megahackathon.

name: LA Hacks (UCLA)
notes: UCLA hackathon with generous travel for out-of-state students.

name: Hack the North (Waterloo)
ticketNote: Free; housing + meals provided, limited travel
notes: Canada's largest collegiate hackathon, 1000 hackers.

name: HackHarvard
notes: Harvard's lively debut-event hackathon.

name: MHacks (Michigan)
notes: Big Midwestern hackathon back on the circuit.

name: hackNY (Fellowship)
notes: Not a weekend hack — a paid NYC startup summer fellowship with a hackday.

name: CityHacks (London)
notes: Student-run London hackathon with a hardware track.

name: TechTogether
notes: Inclusive hackathon series with strong sponsor mentorship.

name: MIT Reality Hack
notes: AR/VR/embodied-AI hack week with industry sponsors — robotics-adjacent.

name: NASA Space Apps Challenge
notes: NASA's worldwide civic hackathon — find a local node, join a team.

name: ICPC World Finals
notes: Competitive programming world finals. Your school registers the team.

name: MIT Battlecode
ticketNote: Free; finals in person at MIT
notes: Realtime robot programming game. Perfect ice-breaker for robotics/eng interviews.

name: Kaggle Competitions
notes: Ongoing ML competitions — small hidden ones feed directly into internships.

name: ARC-AGI Prize
notes: $1M ARC-AGI benchmark — winning it is a recruiting rocket.

name: iCTF (UCSB)
notes: The original attack-defense CTF. Join a campus team.

name: Meta Hacker Cup
notes: Meta's algorithm competition with a paid travel final.

name: Student Cluster Competition (SC)
ticketNote: Team competition — students build a cluster live
notes: Build + tune an HPC cluster under power limits at SC. Great resume line.

name: Google Summer of Code
notes: Not a conference — a stipended open-source summer. Best offline 'event' for interns.

name: Hacktoberfest
notes: Monthly open-source push — small OSS contributions snowball into offers.

name: Advent of Code
notes: 25 days of tough puzzles — great fun and a talking point in interviews.

name: NeurIPS competitions & challenges
notes: NeurIPS hosts side challenges — winning one is a recruiting rocket.

name: Hackster.io challenges
notes: Hardware + embedded design challenges that look great in internship apps.
